items.title: Alan Broadbent interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 26, 2023
items.q: whatever I learned from Johnny Mandel and everybody else

ctx.x: Okay. We’ll come back to it. Yeah. The part of orchestrating, I’m wondering if you have, let me ask you about do you have two favorite things. First of all do you have favorite doublings of a melody? Combinations of instruments that you particularly like because they sound like one new instrument or something?

Yeah well you see that’s where Mahler comes in. That’s what I really — whatever I learned from Johnny Mandel and everybody else, now it began the time of refining my ear and where Mahler, say in a particular passage in the violins while he’s got this beautiful counterpoint going and you’re following it all in this violin passage. Suddenly — not suddenly but somehow it becomes an oboe, and it’s like transitioned into this other sound while all this other movement under this beautiful movement is going. So it’s…
Wow. That’s powerful. I don’t know if you can answer this — say it again?
